question: What is the minimum temperature at which a solid melts to become liquid at the atmospheric pressure known as?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Melting point**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Melting point** is defined as the **minimum temperature** at which a **solid** substance changes its state to **liquid** at standard **atmospheric pressure**.
 
• At the melting point, the **solid and liquid phases** of a substance exist in **thermodynamic equilibrium**, meaning both states can coexist simultaneously without a net change in the amount of either phase.
 
• The melting point of a solid is an indication of the **strength of the force of attraction** between its constituent particles; substances with stronger intermolecular forces generally possess a **higher melting point**.
